traps.shape: a client-supplied temporary-file value joined onto the server scratch path and registered for removal before it is opened
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: this is the advisory's own surface

traps.shape: a client-derived identifier whose decoded path ends in a parent segment survives the lexical in-root prefix test because the normaliser collapses only a segment followed by a separator
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the in-root check is already present and commented, which is why its normalisation gap is easy to dismiss

traps.shape: a name that is not a single path component (a separator plus parent segments) joined verbatim onto the target folder; the default name policy only rejects a leading dot
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: every create/rename already calls the name policy, so the absence of a path-component rule reads as intended design

stacking.notes: T2 (Windows backslash separator) is excluded: it is not observable on the POSIX grader, and requiring a backslash refusal there would over-refuse legitimate names. T5 from the reader record (clipboard-upload name override) is a second route into T4's sink, not an independent concept; the upload security test covers it. The score flag 'single-trap-carries' is inherent to the reader's chosen design (T1 is rated easy), so the stack's difficulty rests on the two hard concepts; the per-concept miss patches prove a fix that misses any one of the three still fails.
